statement: Correction to hypothesis S-da756c80d7: its mechanism is wrong. The clauses {0,1,2},{0,1,3},{0,2,3} give over GF(3) x1=x2=x3 (not pairwise triangle constraints with right-hand side 1), and '2(x1+x2+x3)=3' is not the reason. The witness is still unsatisfiable, checked by hand over 0/1: x1=x2=x3=0 forces x0=1, then {0,4,5} gives x4=x5=0, and {1,2,4} needs x4=1 (contradiction); x1=x2=x3=1 gives x0+2=1, impossible over the integers. Reformulation: because 0/1 triple sums are in {0,1,2,3}, sum≡1 mod 3 with 0/1 entries means sum=1, so sat iff the GF(3) affine solution set meets {0,1}^n. Test in progress: whether a coordinate forced to 2 across all GF(3) solutions explains the unsat cases with null3=2 and m=5.

statement: Does the column-sparse branching lemma (S0002, 2^s over s free columns times the rank-r DP) cover entrywise-sparse corrections E with k nonzero entries in total? If each nonzero lies in a column with few such entries, the number of free columns is at most k, so the time would be poly * (2^k) * (nB+1)^r. Test: measure the minimum column-cover size of E on random near-low-rank W, and check whether the time bound beats 2^n when k + r log2(nB+1) <= (1-eps) n.

structure.content: Source check of MMW19 (STOC 2019, people.csail.mit.edu/rrw/MCSP-MKTP-stoc19.pdf), fetched text in this session. Theorem 1.1: uniform AC circuit family for MCSP^A[s(n)] on 2^n-bit inputs of Otilde(2^n * s(n)^2) size and O(n/log l(n)) depth with Sigma3SAT^A oracle gates, for s(n) >= n and l(n) >= s(n)^2. Theorem 1.2: one-pass streaming algorithm for search-MCSP^A[s(n)] on 2^n-bit inputs running in 2^n * Otilde(s(n)) time with Otilde(s(n)^2) update time and Otilde(s(n)) space, using Sigma3SAT^A oracle with queries of length Otilde(s(n)). Theorem 1.3: if some time-constructible s(n) >= n and A in PH make search-MCSP^A[s(n)] unsolvable by a poly(s(n))-space streaming algorithm with poly(s(n)) update time, then P != NP (proof: P = NP answers the Sigma3SAT^A calls of Thm 1.2). The fetched text states Thm 1.2 with update time per stream bit, matching the reading recorded for Q-b241b9d778. Not checked here: the proofs of Thm 1.1 and 1.2 in Sections 3-4, and whether the Otilde hides only polylog(N) factors.

statement: CROSSING-COUNT TRADE-OFF in Viola's decomposition (Q-5226caddf1, step 1, sub-question). Setting: time-t one-tape q-state DTM on N input cells, crossing count c_j = number of head crossings of the boundary between cells j and j+1 (sum_j c_j <= t). Verified arithmetic: Markov gives that at most N/2 cells have c_j > 2t/N, so half the cells are 'cheap' (c_j <= 2t/N). Verified obstacle: choosing cut points only among cheap cells and guessing their crossing sequences gives a sum of (tq)^{sum of chosen c_j} terms, which can be exp(t) when all N cells are cut; the union bound then costs seed about t log q, far above N^{mu'}. Viola's sqrt(t) is consistent with a balance between the number of cuts k and the crossings per cut: total guess exponent about k*t/N (averaged) against maximal width exponent about max c_j. Open: is there a cut set with k = N^{o(1)} pieces, total guess exponent <= t^{eps}, and max c_j <= t^{eps} simultaneously? CONJECTURE, not proved; the claim of a sqrt(t) lower bound for this decomposition is not established.

statement: H-INFO-001 (owner 2026-11-19: not a new time definition, but WHICH information a computation needs WHEN). For a positive 1-in-3 formula F and a variable order, at each cut t (processed vs unprocessed variables) compare three counts: (a) N_exact(t) = number of distinct residual Boolean functions F|alpha over all partial assignments alpha (Myhill-Nerode; the information the decision truly needs at t), (b) N_front(t) = number of reachable frontier-clause states (which partly assigned clauses already hold a 1; the obvious DP state, an upper bound), (c) N_gf3(t) = number of distinct GF(3) residual syndromes (lossy). Questions: (1) is N_exact < N_front on some instances, i.e. does the obvious state carry superfluous information, and what is dropped? (2) on GF(3)-blind cores, where exactly does (c) merge classes that (a) separates - is the missing bit always two-valuedness (D-018)? (3) min over orders of max_t log2 N_exact(t) (= OBDD width) on blind cores n<=9 vs SAT controls and 2-SAT/XOR: does it grow with n on the blind family? Exact enumeration, n<=9; long runs as desk jobs.

statement: Why the stage decomposition in S0016/S0017 is forced: a single unrolled circuit for the whole run has T = N*u steps, but each step must select the input bit at the RAM's read counter, which costs N per step (N-way multiplexer over x), giving N^2*u*poly(S*w), not N*u*poly(S*w). Only a stage whose input bit x_{i+1} is a fixed wire avoids the N-way selection. So Lemma 12 (Gamma <= 2^m*poly(s)) needs a fixed stage per read with size independent of x. Under only the amortised premise sum_i t_i(x) <= N*u, the per-stage size must be max_x t_i(x), which can be N*u for one i, giving N^2*u. Candidate repair (carry a backlog of unfinished steps into the next stage) fails: a stage that stalls must hand forward a pending read bit x_j that is consumed later, so the carried state is a queue of input bits, breaking the poly(S*w) state bound. Open: whether the backlog stays bounded under sum_i t_i <= N*u with t_i >= 1 (each read takes at least one step). If the backlog is O(1) per stage, the repair works; if not, it fails. The primary-text definition of update time (G0002) decides which premise MMW Thm 1.2 gives.

A degree-2 PC refutation for every GF(3)-blind UNSAT positive 1-in-3 formula would give polynomial-size, polynomially checkable refutations for that family. Even a uniform degree bound d only gives an n^O(d) procedure for the blind class, which is a restricted-class statement, not a general lower or upper bound.

The features I used (pts, n_value2, ndeg, pair counts) do not capture this. Is the Boolean-feasibility of the 9-point plane a target-free function of the clause-incidence structure, and does the blind subclass coincide with a fixed pattern of 2-level lines covering the plane? This is a reformulation of the sat definition on the solution set, so it is not by itself a separator. The open point is whether a combinatorial invariant of the clauses computes it without solving the linear system.
